title: The Scrambler

scenario.title: Scrambled copy people still have to read
scenario.body: Designers scramble text to test a layout, and teachers use it for the "your brain still reads it" trick. The book's word pattern only knows A to Z, so "crème brûlée" and "привет" never get scrambled, and it happily turns NASA into NSAA. Keep every seed the book's tests check, and fix those.

tagline: Scramble the octopus juggles the middle letters of every word but never drops the first or last one. Can you still read it? (You probably can!)

brain_blurbs.book: Juggles words made of the letters A to Z.
brain_blurbs.real: Juggles words in any language, and leaves NASA alone.

rules.test_usage: Explains the trick when you ask for help
rules.test_text2: Lucky number 2 juggles the fox sentence exactly like the book
rules.test_file_bustle: Reads a whole poem from a file and keeps its lines
rules.test_file_spiders: "Don't" can become "Do'nt": the ' counts as part of the word
rules.test_other_alphabets_are_words_too: Russian and Greek words get juggled too
rules.test_acronyms_stay_put: NASA and HTML stay NASA and HTML
rules.test_numbers_and_punctuation_stay: Numbers, commas and dots don't move
rules.test_same_letters_first_and_last_kept: Any word: same letters, same first and last letter
rules.test_short_words_untouched: Words of three letters or fewer are never touched
rules.test_only_letters_move: Spaces, numbers, commas and dots stay put
rules.test_seed_means_same_line: Any sentence: the same lucky number gives the same mess

examples: Your brain is amazing at reading
